metadata.title: Johnny Mundt Is Better Left on Waivers
metadata.description: Philadelphia Eagles tight end Johnny Mundt is going to see the field while Dallas Goedert (knee) is out, but that does not make him a strong waiver target. Mundt caught two of three targets for eight yards against Tennessee and played 49 of 76 offensive snaps, already starting alongside Goedert before the injury. The bigger issue is what Philadelphia did next. The Eagles brought Zach Ertz back on the practice squad, and RotoBaller's FAAB column flatly notes that Mundt is not a starter. His history points the same way. Mundt has never reached 200 receiving yards in a season and has only four touchdowns in his NFL career. There may be a random short touchdown while Goedert is sidelined, but the target ceiling is hard to trust, especially if Ertz is elevated for Monday night. Mundt can be monitored in very deep leagues, but most fantasy managers should leave him on waivers and look elsewhere for Week 3 help.

metadata.title: Johnny Mundt - Records two receptions Week 2
metadata.description: Mundt caught two of three targets for eight yards in Sunday's 24-20 win against the Titans.
metadata.analysis: Mundt started along with fellow tight end Dallas Goedert (knee), and he logged 49 of Philadelphia's 76 offensive snaps. The significant playing time was partly due to Goedert exiting in the first half after spraining his MCL. Goedert is now slated to miss multiple weeks due to the injury, but that won't necessarily mean that Mundt will be an attractive fantasy waiver-wire pickup. The Eagles signed veteran Zach Ertz to a contract Tuesday, and he'll likely slide in as the team's top tight end during Goedert's absence, though it's unclear how long Ertz will need to get up to speed.

metadata.title: Johnny Mundt inks one-year deal with Eagles
metadata.description: Tight end Johnny Mundt has agreed to a one-year deal with the Philadelphia Eagles. Mundt was released by the Jaguars earlier in the day.
metadata.analysis: Mundt, a nine-year veteran in the NFL, is widely known more for his blocking than for his pass catching ability. He has never caught more than 19 passes in a single season, doing it twice with the Vikings in 2022 and 2024, and has totaled just 74 catches in 114 career games. In his lone season with Jacksonville last year, Mundt caught nine passes for 111 yards in 16 games. With the addition of Mundt and the return of Grant Calcaterra, the Eagles are making sure to cover their bases in the event Dallas Goedert leaves. If that is the case, Calcaterra would likely start and handle the catching duties while Mundt would play in two tight end sets as an additional blocker.

metadata.title: Johnny Mundt - Packs bags for Philly
metadata.description: Mundt agreed to terms Tuesday on a one-year contract with the Eagles, Mike Garafolo of NFL Network reports.
metadata.analysis: Mundt quickly found a new home after being released by the Jaguars on Monday. The 31-year-old tight end played 385 offensive snaps last season but mostly stuck to a run-blocking role, catching just nine of 19 targets for 111 yards and no touchdowns. At the time of this report, Dallas Goedert still hasn't re-signed with the team, but the Eagles did sign Grant Calcaterra to a one-year deal, according to Jeff McLane of The Philadelphia Inquirer. Mundt should be a key blocking piece to the Eagles' run-heavy attack, which frequently utilizes multiple tight ends, in 2026 regardless of Goedert's status with the team.

metadata.title: Eagles Agree to a One-Year Deal With Johnny Mundt
metadata.description: The Philadelphia Eagles have signed tight end Johnny Mundt to a one-year deal, according to Mike Garafolo of NFL Network. Mundt is primarily known for his blocking, as he caught just nine passes and scored zero touchdowns across 16 games with the Jacksonville Jaguars in 2025. Released by the Jaguars last week, Mundt possesses nine years of NFL experience with stops in Los Angeles (Rams), Minnesota, and Jacksonville. He'll offer much-needed depth for the Eagles, who entered this offseason with their top three tight ends slated for free agency. Philadelphia already re-signed Grant Calcaterra, but Dallas Goedert and Kylen Granson are still unrestricted free agents. If neither Goedert nor Granson returns, Mundt would slot in as the team's No. 2 tight end, at least for the time being. Even so, his proficiency as a blocker limits his receiving upside and keeps him off the fantasy radar in most leagues.

metadata.title: Johnny Mundt released by Jaguars
metadata.description: The Jaguars released TE Johnny Mundt
metadata.analysis: Mundt should draw some interest in free agency as a primary blocking tight end.

metadata.title: Johnny Mundt - Let go by Jacksonville
metadata.description: The Jaguars released Mundt on Monday, Tom Pelissero of NFL Network reports.
metadata.analysis: Mundt signed a two-year deal with the Jaguars in March of 2025 after spending the three prior years with the Vikings, but his time in Jacksonville will end after just one season. He caught nine passes (on 19 targets) for 111 yards across 16 regular-season games in 2025, when he served mostly as a run blocker and as a backup to Brenton Strange. Now that he's a free agent, Mundt should garner interest from teams looking to add a depth tight end who can serve as an extra blocker.

metadata.title: Johnny Mundt - Secures one pass Week 18
metadata.description: Mundt caught his only target for 16 yards during Sunday's 41-7 win against the Titans.
metadata.analysis: The 31-year-old's 16-yard reception during the second quarter was his first catch since Week 12 in Arizona. Mundt played in 16 games this season while serving as a secondary tight end for the Jaguars, and he finished the regular season with nine catches for 111 yards. He's under contract with Jacksonville for 2026, but he carries a $3.25 million cap hit could be released with just a $500,000 dead cap penalty.

metadata.title: Johnny Mundt - Healthy scratch Week 14
metadata.description: Mundt (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against Indianapolis.
metadata.analysis: Mundt is healthy, but he's going to miss his first game of the season. The veteran tight end has produced eight catches on 17 targets for 95 yards through 12 games on the campaign. Mundt appears to be fourth in the Jaguars' tight-end pecking order behind Brenton Strange, Quintin Morris and Hunter Long.

metadata.title: Johnny Mundt - Notches two receptions
metadata.description: Mundt caught two of three targets for 25 yards during Sunday's 35-6 win against the Chargers.
metadata.analysis: The 30-year-old played 41 of 71 offensive snaps in the absences of Hunter Long (hip) and Brenton Strange (hip), while Quintin Morris led the way for Jacksonville's tight ends with 50 snaps. Mundt now has seven catches for 83 yards through 10 games this season and is likely to continue being sporadically involved in the Jaguars' aerial attack.
